interface.name: tahoe_glass_manager_v1
interface.description:
This private protocol lets a client describe exact rounded glass regions for a wl_surface. The compositor owns blur, tint, refraction, clipping, and shadow rendering for those regions.
The manager version is kept in lockstep with tahoe_glass_surface_v1 so that surface objects (which inherit the manager's bound version) can negotiate the presentation-transform requests added in version 4 and the serial-correlated completion feedback added in version 5.

request.name: get_tahoe_glass_surface

description.summary: create a glass region controller for a surface

request.description: The returned object stores pending glass regions for the supplied wl_surface. Pending state is committed together with the next wl_surface commit.

interface.name: tahoe_glass_surface_v1
interface.description:
Regions are double-buffered and committed with the associated wl_surface. Region coordinates are surface-local logical coordinates.
Since version 4 the surface also carries an optional presentation transform: a translate + per-axis scale the compositor applies when rendering the surface and its glass regions. The transform is presentation-only — it never affects input, layout, or the protocol region geometry itself, and the compositor may restrict it to layer-shell surfaces.
Since version 5 clients can tag a presentation-transform request with a serial and receive exactly one terminal feedback event. This closes the animation lifecycle without changing the version 4 request signatures.

entry.name: invalid_serial
entry.summary: transform serial is zero or already in flight

entry.name: clip
entry.summary: clip effect to the rounded region

request.name: set_region

description.summary: set or update a rounded glass region

request.description:
If a region with the same id already exists, it is replaced. Otherwise a new region is appended, up to the compositor limit.
The interaction scalar (0..1) drives compositor-side material easing so a region can intensify its glass (higher highlight, refraction, inner shadow) during hover, press, or enter animations. 0 means at rest.
The material alpha scalar (0..1) fades compositor material parameters without changing the region bounds. Clients use it for popup/backdrop enter and exit transitions while keeping geometry stable.

description.summary: remove one pending region by id

entry.name: completed
entry.summary: the tagged transform reached its terminal value

entry.name: rejected
entry.summary: the tagged transform could not be applied

entry.name: superseded
entry.summary: a newer transform replaced the tagged transform

entry.name: cancelled
entry.summary: the tagged transform was cancelled by lifecycle teardown

request.name: set_transform
request.description:
Double-buffered; applied on the next wl_surface commit. Sets the presentation transform to translate (x, y) + per-axis scale (scale_x, scale_y), cancelling any running transform animation. (0, 0, 1, 1) restores the identity transform.
The transform maps surface-local logical coordinates: a surface point p renders at surface_position + (x, y) + (scale_x * p.x, scale_y * p.y). Scales are clamped into [0.05, 20] and translations into [-16384, 16384].
At most one transform request (set_transform, set_transform_target or set_region_morph) takes effect per commit; the last one wins.

request.name: set_transform_target

description.summary: animate the presentation transform to a target

request.description:
Double-buffered; applied on the next wl_surface commit. Starts a compositor-side animation of the presentation transform from its current value to the given target. Spring curves carry over velocity when retargeting a running animation; eased curves restart from the current value without velocity. Once the animation settles on the identity transform the surface renders untransformed again.
curve selects the animation curve. For spring, params are p1 = damping ratio, p2 = stiffness, p3 = epsilon (progress space); p4 and p5 are reserved and must be 0. For eased, params are p1 = duration in ms and p2..p5 = cubic-bezier control points x1, y1, x2, y2.
Value ranges and the last-one-wins rule match set_transform.

arg.name: x
arg.summary: target translation x in logical px

arg.name: y
arg.summary: target translation y in logical px

arg.name: p1
arg.summary: spring damping ratio, or eased duration ms

request.name: set_region_morph

description.summary: animate a region geometry change as a container morph

request.description:
Double-buffered; applied on the next wl_surface commit. When that commit changes the rectangle of the region with the given id from R_old to R_new, the compositor starts a presentation-transform animation from the affine that maps R_new onto the current visual footprint of R_old (its rectangle under the presentation transform in effect just before the commit) and animates to identity.
This lets a client commit content laid out for the new geometry in a single atomic commit while the compositor performs the morph, including correct continuation when a morph is retargeted mid-flight.
If the region does not exist on both sides of the commit, or its rectangle is unchanged, the request is discarded. Curve arguments match set_transform_target; the last-one-wins rule applies.

arg.name: region_id
arg.summary: glass region id to anchor the morph on

arg.name: p1
arg.summary: spring damping ratio, or eased duration ms

request.name: set_transform_serial
request.description:
Associates serial with the next set_transform, set_transform_target, or set_region_morph request sent on this object. The tag is consumed by that request and applied with the same wl_surface commit.
A client must use a non-zero serial that it has not reused for another in-flight transform on this object; violating either rule raises the invalid_serial protocol error. Replacing an unconsumed tag or a tagged transform that has not completed produces superseded feedback for the older serial. A tag not followed by a transform before the next wl_surface commit is rejected.
Version 1 through 4 clients do not use this request and retain the original silent last-one-wins behavior.

event.name: capabilities

description.summary: feedback capabilities supported by the compositor

event.description: Sent once when the surface controller is created. A client must wait for this event and confirm the transform_feedback capability before relying on terminal events.

event.name: transform_feedback

description.summary: terminal state for one tagged transform

event.description: Sent exactly once for every accepted non-zero serial while this protocol object remains alive. Replacing an unconsumed tag produces superseded feedback; committing one without a transform produces rejected feedback. completed is emitted only after an animated transform settles (or immediately after a non-animated transform is applied). rejected, superseded, and cancelled are terminal and must not later be followed by completed for the same serial. Destroying this protocol object precludes further wire feedback.
